issues.body: The round-5 major finding remains materially unchanged. Store.validateStore and InitOutput.store_validateStore are added to the generated declaration file, but the checkout contains no corresponding Rust/wasm implementation or generated JavaScript binding. This lets TypeScript consumers compile a validateStore call that will fail because the method/export is absent at runtime. Generated wasm-bindgen declarations must match the shipped runtime artifacts.
issues.fix_hint: Remove the validateStore documentation, method declaration, cross-link, and InitOutput export from this PR. If the API is intended, implement it in the wasm source, add focused stateful/default-graph equivalence tests, update the matching public JS/WASM skill, and regenerate all wasm-bindgen artifacts rather than editing only the declaration file.
issues.title: Generated typings still declare validateStore without a runtime implementation

verdict.summary: Round 6 is stagnant. The same major issue from round 5 remains: the diff advertises Store.validateStore and the low-level store_validateStore export only in the generated TypeScript declaration, while no corresponding Rust/wasm implementation or generated JavaScript runtime binding exists. TypeScript consumers can compile against an API that is absent at runtime. The file-ingest refactor and its focused picker tests appear coherent, but they do not resolve this blocking declaration/runtime mismatch.
